about.title: Scholarships and jobs, matched with reasons.
about.lede: Built for people who are tired of scrolling generic boards. Enter what you’ve studied and what you can do — we rank openings and say why they fit.
about.ideaTitle: Matching should feel like a briefing, not a dump of links.
about.ideaBody1: Search engines and opportunity boards show volume. They rarely know your Computer Science degree, your React skills, or that you’re applying from Botswana — and they almost never explain the fit.
about.ideaBody2: Opportunistic keeps one living profile and runs scholarship and job matching against it. Every result carries a score, a source, and a reason you can actually use.
about.p1Body: Degrees, skills, and country are the source of truth. Matches rebuild when you change them.
about.p2Body: A score without an explanation is noise. We write why a listing fits — in plain language.
about.p3Body: We discover and rank. You apply on the official scholarship or employer site.
about.areItem2: Playbook tips unique to your skills and goals
about.areItem3: Save, dismiss, and rematch when your profile changes

about.notItem3: Always verify deadlines on the official listing

privacyBody.overview: Opportunistic (“we”) provides scholarship and job matching. This policy explains what we collect, why, how long we keep it, and your rights. We apply a GDPR-grade baseline for every user worldwide, and we respect stricter local rules where they apply (including UK GDPR, POPIA in South Africa, and similar frameworks). This is practical compliance guidance for our product — not formal legal advice for your jurisdiction.
privacyBody.lawfulContractDesc: Creating your account, matching, and delivering the service you request
privacyBody.lawfulConsentDesc: Optional cookies (analytics/marketing), email digests you opt into
privacyBody.lawfulLegitimateDesc: Security, abuse prevention, service reliability — balanced against your rights
privacyBody.lawfulLegalDesc: Where we must retain or disclose data under applicable law
privacyBody.storeAccountDesc: Email and auth credentials via Supabase Auth
privacyBody.storeProfileDesc: Name, country, headline, bio, qualifications, and skills you enter
privacyBody.storeMatchesDesc: Title, URL, source, reasoning, score, and save/dismiss state
privacyBody.storeTechnicalDesc: Consent cookie, session cookies needed for login, optional analytics if you allow them
privacyBody.cookiesIntro: We use a consent cookie (opp_consent) to remember your choice for up to 12 months. Necessary cookies keep authentication secure. Preferences, analytics, and marketing cookies load only after you opt in. You can change your mind anytime.
privacyBody.cookiesNecessaryDesc: Auth session, security, storing this consent
privacyBody.cookiesAnalyticsDesc: Usage measurement — scripts blocked until allowed
privacyBody.cookiesMarketingDesc: Ad / remarketing tags — scripts blocked until allowed
privacyBody.cookiesOrFooter: — or use Cookie settings in the footer.
privacyBody.useBody: Your profile powers matching and reasoned tips. We do not sell personal data. We do not use your qualifications to build advertising profiles unless you explicitly allow marketing cookies and a future ad partner is disclosed here.
privacyBody.transfersBody: Infrastructure may process data in regions used by our providers (for example Supabase and Brevo). Where data leaves your country, we rely on appropriate safeguards recognized under GDPR-style rules (such as standard contractual clauses offered by those providers) and minimize what we store.
privacyBody.retentionBody: Account and match data stay while your account is active. If you delete your data in Settings, we remove profile, qualifications, skills, matches, and search history from the app database. Auth-account purge may also be requested at hello@opportunistic.online. Consent records may be kept as proof of choice for up to the cookie lifetime or as required by law.
privacyBody.rightsBody: Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object, port data, and withdraw consent. We honour these as a global baseline. You can edit your profile anytime and delete your data from Settings.
privacyBody.rightsCalloutMid: → Delete my data. For other requests:
privacyBody.childrenBody: Opportunistic is not directed at children under 16 (or the higher digital-consent age in your country). Do not create an account if you are under that age. If we learn we hold such data, we will delete it.
privacyBody.sharingBody: We share data with processors who help run the service: Supabase (auth/database), Brevo (transactional email when enabled), and hosting (GitHub Pages). Listings open on third-party sites with their own policies. We do not sell personal data.

termsBody.roleBody: Opportunistic is a discovery platform. We surface third-party scholarship and job listings based on your profile. We are not the issuer, employer, or grantor of any opportunity shown on the site.
termsBody.roleCallout: Always finish applications on the official source listing. Opportunistic explains fit; the source owns eligibility and outcomes.
termsBody.accuracyBody: Listings can become outdated after indexing. Always verify eligibility, deadlines, and application steps on the source website before applying. Match scores, reasoning, and tips are advisory — they are not guarantees of acceptance, funding, or employment.
termsBody.accountAccuracyDesc: You are responsible for the truthfulness of information you submit
termsBody.accountOthersDesc: Do not upload someone else’s personal data without permission
termsBody.accountFairDesc: We may suspend accounts that abuse matching or attempt to scrape the service
termsBody.liabilityBody: To the fullest extent permitted by law, Opportunistic is not liable for decisions made based on surfaced listings, including closed opportunities, inaccurate third-party content, or unsuccessful applications.

tips.sLeadership: Write a 150-word leadership story that starts in {{place}} and ends with how a {{source}} award multiplies that impact.
tips.sModules: Map your {{field}} background to 3 modules on a target {{location}} program — name the modules in your personal statement.
tips.sEssaySkills: In essay 1, dedicate one paragraph to how {{skills}} already produced a measurable result (numbers beat adjectives).
tips.sAdvanced: Lead with your {{skill}} depth ({{level}}) as proof you can handle {{intensity}} intensity.
tips.sWeak: Before submitting, raise {{skill}} with a short project or certificate — reviewers notice unfinished skill claims.
tips.sRefereeInst: Ask a referee from {{institution}} who saw you lead, not only teach you — Chevening-style panels weight influence over grades alone.
tips.sRefereeGeneric: Secure two referees who can quote a specific initiative you ran — vague “hardworking student” letters sink strong profiles.
tips.sCalendar: Build a deadline reverse calendar from “{{deadline}}” with buffers for transcripts, tests, and references.
tips.sOffline: Draft answers offline first, then paste into the portal — auto-save glitches erase hours of work on many scholarship forms.
tips.sAlumni: Research 2 alumni from {{place}} who won {{source}}; note what their applications emphasized and mirror the structure, not the story.
tips.sScore: If your match score is {{score}}%, treat gaps honestly in the essay — panels reward self-awareness more than perfection claims.
tips.sHeadline: Align your headline (“{{headline}}”) with the program’s stated mission so the first screen already feels intentional.
tips.sPitch: Prepare a 60-second verbal pitch of your study plan for interviews: problem → your edge → {{source}} as the accelerator.
tips.sProof: Collect proof artifacts (GitHub, reports, awards, community letters) that back every skill you listed — screenshots ready before you apply.
tips.sEligibility: Check nationality and return-home clauses for {{source}} against your {{country}} status this cycle — eligibility mistakes waste strong essays.
tips.sBio: Rewrite your bio so a stranger in {{location}} understands your field in one sentence, then expand.
tips.sCheveningCourses: Pick three UK courses that genuinely fit {{field}}, not prestige alone — Chevening rejects mismatched course trios even with strong essays.
tips.sCheveningNet: Spend a full page on “networking” plans: which UK societies, labs, or policy groups you will join, and what you bring back to {{place}}.
tips.sDaadFilter: Filter DAAD by your exact degree level and {{field}}, then shortlist 2 calls — generic “Germany” applications rarely clear the first cut.
tips.sDaadLang: Decide early whether you need German or English proof for the host program, and book the test date before the call closes.
tips.sMastercardApply: Apply through a partner university that teaches {{field}} — Mastercard Scholars is campus-specific, not one global form.
tips.sMastercardNeed: Document need and leadership together: one paragraph on barriers, one on what you already changed for others in {{place}}.
tips.sFulbrightPage: Use your country’s Fulbright page only — deadlines and forms for {{country}} differ from the global brochure.
tips.sFulbrightObj: Make the research/study objective falsifiable: what question in {{field}} will you answer in 12–24 months?
tips.sGates: Cambridge fit comes first: name a supervisor or lab group relevant to {{field}} before polishing the Gates statement.
tips.sTheme: Tie your proposal to a published theme from {{source}}, using language from the call — thematic misalignment is a common silent reject.
tips.jResume: Rewrite your résumé summary to lead with {{skill}} + {{field}}, then mirror the top 5 verbs from each {{source}} posting you open.
tips.jProof: Build a 1-page “proof sheet” with 3 bullets: problem, action using {{skills}}, measurable result.
tips.jAdvanced: Put {{skills}} in the first third of your LinkedIn/About — recruiters skim, they don’t hunt.
tips.jWeak: For roles requiring {{skill}}, add a weekend mini-project and link it — intermediate claims without evidence get filtered out.
tips.jAlerts: Set {{source}} alerts for “{{field}}” and your country ({{country}}), then apply within 48 hours of posting.
tips.jTarget: Target 5 companies per week that hire for {{field}} in or from {{country}}, not 50 random Easy Apply clicks.
tips.jCover: In every cover note, name one concrete deliverable you would ship in the first 30 days using your current stack.
tips.jReferrals: Ask for referrals only after you can explain the team’s product in 2 sentences — cold asks without homework burn bridges.
tips.jLoom: Record a 90-second Loom (or voice note) walking through a project; attach it when {{source}} allows message/apply extras.
tips.jConfidence: Your current match confidence is ~{{score}}% — if under 70%, tighten skills on Profile and rematch before spraying applications.
tips.jTranslate: Translate academic language from {{field}} into employer language: “coursework” → “delivered X under deadline”.
tips.jLog: Keep a rejection log: role, missing skill, next action — patterns tell you what to learn next faster than guesswork.
tips.jLinkedinOpen: Turn on Open to Work (recruiters only) and pin a featured project that proves {{skill}}.
tips.jLinkedinComment: Comment thoughtfully on 3 hiring-manager posts in {{field}} this week before cold-applying — warm visibility beats silent Apply.
tips.jIndeed: Use Indeed’s location filter exactly as “{{country}}” and sort by date — stale reposts waste energy.
tips.jRemoteOk: Read the country/timezone line twice on Remote OK posts — many “remote” roles still exclude {{country}}.
tips.jRemoteRate: Price your contractor rate and timezone overlap upfront in the first message to avoid ghosting after screens.
tips.jGlassdoor: Read the latest interview reports for that employer, then prepare 2 stories that answer the most repeated question pattern.
tips.jReliefImpact: Lead applications with field/volunteer impact in {{place}} — ReliefWeb hiring heavily weights mission-relevant experience.
tips.jReliefLang: Match language from the vacancy (MEAL, protection, WASH, etc.) only if you can defend it — buzzword stuffing is obvious.
tips.jHeadline: Sync your public headline to “{{headline}}” everywhere you apply so {{source}} screens and your CV tell one story.
